title: Widgets: product's plan, ECharts and build 8
intro: I compared product's widget plan (`product/design/widget-*.md` and `query-visuals.md`) with build 8's design (`docs/plans/build-8-design.md` §1) and what harness has today (table, CSS bars, value; no chart library). Each question has my recommendation; **Take the recommendations** if you agree and change the few you don't. **Blocking** ones decide the contracts, so I need them first. Build 8 is already building widgets from the current design; your answers will be applied as a focused pass on top of it.

content.title: Where build 8's design differs from product's plan
content.md:
| Product | Build 8 design | |
|---|---|---|
| Widget = fn of kind `widget`, renders in chat | `hub/widget` kind, `WidgetSpec` | same |
| Rich gate: column facts (grouped vs measure, distinct counts, ranges, ids) + rules | required column kinds, row range, `whole` | much thinner |
| Ranking: most columns shown wins, then priority; non-fits shown greyed with why | client score 0..1, non-fits hidden | different |
| 13 families with styles (bar/stacked/100%…) | table, bar, value | missing |
| Size strategies: top-N, "Other" slice | — | missing |
| Buffered pager (fetch 50, page locally) | each page is a run | different |
| Choices as label + value, presets, relative dates | plain values, no presets | missing |
| A chart can drive range args (calendar, zoom) | — | missing |
| Form counts as the confirm (no double prompt) | form, then confirm | different |
| After an action: derived from what it returns; drill-down stack | author says refresh/show/none; no drill | different |
| Read-only view for results of writes | — | missing |
| Strict per-call authoring schema; proposes, you save | check loop; agent saves | different |
| Routing line derived from each fn's return type; run after authoring | instruction prose | different |
| Renderer tiers, no system JS in the browser | trusted Vue visuals in one hub registry | harness better |
| Realtime refresh, streamed export, dashboards | — | both later |

content.title: What I'd take, and what I wouldn't
content.md:
**Take:** declared richer matching judged on the hub; coverage-first ranking with greyed non-fits; families with styles on ECharts `dataset`+`encode`; honest partial data (whole-only visuals withheld, "Showing N of M", top-N + Other); buffered pager; labelled choices, presets, relative dates, range claims; confirm without a double prompt and derived result routing; drill-down; read-only write results; a short model summary of widget runs; product's ECharts rules (own lazy chunk, one `use()`, `setTheme`, SVG, `outerBounds`, coarse pointer, clicks via `dataIndex`); full screen and image download.

**Don't take:** product's renderer tiers / no-system-JS (harness already decided trusted Vue visuals); gates as code the hub runs (use declarative rules); multi-source widgets and shape memory in localStorage; product's ORM machinery; aggregation in the browser over a partial page (breaks "no in-memory filtering"); realtime, streamed export, dashboards, map/geo charts this build.

questions.question: How does a visual declare the data it can draw?
questions.why: The core contract every lane builds on.

content.code:
VisualShape = {
  channels: [{ name, label, accepts: ColumnKind[], facet?, required, many, role?: 'group'|'measure' }],
  rows: { min, max? }, whole: boolean,
  rules?: ('keysDistinct'|'nonNegative'|'oneRowPerKey'|'acyclic'|'declaredMax'|'unaggregated')[],
  strategy?: 'window'|'top-n'|'partition'|'aggregate',
  subTypes?: { name, label, whole? }[],
  claims?: 'range',
  priority: number,
}
